snippet.title: My First Time Watching Football with Brazilians | They Are Absolutely CRAZY! ⚽
snippet.description:
📍My First Time Watching Football with Brazilians – They Are Absolutely CRAZY! 🇧🇷⚽

Today I experienced something I'll never forget. I watched the Brazil vs Japan FIFA World Cup 2026 match surrounded by Brazilian fans, and the atmosphere was unbelievable!

The moment Brazil scored, the entire place exploded with celebration. People were singing, shouting, hugging strangers, waving flags, and celebrating as if they had known each other for years. It wasn't just a football match—it was a national celebration.

In Brazil, football is more than a sport; it's part of the culture and everyday life. During important matches, many schools close, shops shut down, offices pause work, and millions of people gather with friends and family to support the Seleção. The passion and unity I witnessed were unlike anything I've ever experienced.

As a Pakistani living in Brazil, this was my first time watching a football match with Brazilians, and I finally understood why Brazil is known around the world as the country of football.

If you love football, Brazil should definitely be on your travel bucket list!

snippet.title: Greece Digital Nomad Visa 🇬🇷 | Step-by-Step Guide for Pakistani Passport Holders (2026)
snippet.description:
Want to move to Greece on a Pakistani passport as a remote worker, freelancer, or online business owner? In this video, Sufyan Abroad explains the Greece Digital Nomad Visa, who can apply, income requirement, documents, and the step-by-step process for Pakistani applicants.

The Greece Digital Nomad Visa is for non-EU remote workers who work for companies, clients, or businesses outside Greece. It usually allows an initial stay of up to 12 months, with the option to apply for a longer residence permit after arrival.


What You’ll Learn
What is the Greece Digital Nomad Visa
Eligibility for Pakistani passport holders
Remote employee vs freelancer requirements
Minimum income requirement: around €3,500/month
Required documents checklist
Step-by-step application process
Family members and income increase
Common mistakes to avoid

Basic Requirements
Valid Pakistani passport
Remote job, freelance clients, or foreign business
Work must be for employers/clients outside Greece
Proof of monthly income
Health insurance
Clean criminal record
Accommodation proof in Greece
Visa application form and supporting documents

Step-by-Step Process
Check your eligibility as a remote worker or freelancer.
Prepare work proof: employment contract, client contracts, or business documents.
Collect income proof and bank statements.
Arrange health insurance and accommodation proof.
Prepare police clearance and translations if required.
Book appointment with the Greek Embassy/Consulate.
Submit your application and pay the visa fee.
Wait for processing and decision.
Travel to Greece after approval.
Apply for residence permit if you plan to stay longer.
Important Note

You are not allowed to work for Greek employers or local Greek clients under this visa. Your income should come from outside Greece.

This video is for educational purposes only. Visa rules, income thresholds, fees, and processing times may change. Always verify with the official Greek Embassy or immigration authority before applying.

snippet.title: ¿Te llama la policía? El error que muchos inmigrantes cometen
snippet.description:
Recibes una llamada de la policía y te piden acudir a comisaría.

La reacción más habitual suele ser pensar que se trata de una simple comprobación y que lo mejor es acudir cuanto antes para resolverlo.

Sin embargo, esa misma confianza es la que en ocasiones termina generando problemas.

Porque no todas las llamadas tienen la misma importancia.

Y no todas las situaciones tienen las mismas consecuencias jurídicas.

Por eso existe una recomendación que repetimos constantemente en extranjería:

Antes de acudir, entiende qué está pasando.

Hablar con un abogado no significa ocultar información ni dejar de colaborar.

Significa conocer tus derechos, entender el contexto y evitar errores provocados por los nervios o la improvisación.

La mayoría de los problemas no aparecen porque una persona quiera hacer algo mal.

Aparecen porque nadie le explicó qué debía hacer antes de actuar.
